how_to_read: Each case names the rows of the page's decision table it rests on (`rests_on`) and its release (`release`): `0.1.0` for what step 2 of the local-first 0.1.0 builds, `0.2.0` for a part the owner moved to 0.2.0, kept as written on Nov 24. A case on an open Q row holds the recommended option. `rule` names the rule of the page that gives `expect` from `input`, written plainly in sdk/tests/test_wave_an_contract.py; a case with no rule is a requirement its paths' targets test. `paths`: `rule` (checked here on every tree), `http` (the read API, a target), `server` (the server's start or a restart, a target), `python` (the SDK's readers: a pin or a target). Keys in a listing are relative to the rank folder `runs/<run_id>/rank=<rank>/`. Ages are hours before the rules' clock.

cases.name: catalog_rebuild_reasons
cases.why: Section 1.5's table: what a server does with the catalog file it finds at start.

cases.name: catalog_never_ahead_of_store
cases.why: An event is sent only after its object is stored, so a crash leaves the catalog behind the store, never ahead of it, and the resync at the next start brings it level.

cases.name: catalog_place
cases.why: Section 1.2: the state folder on a local disk; the per-user temporary folder when the state folder is on a network filesystem or its type cannot be read; off, and said, when neither can be used; --catalog off; a named path refused under the store root or on a network filesystem.

cases.name: api_runs_page
cases.why: /v1/runs pages, newest status first, then run ID; the last page has no token.

cases.name: api_errors
cases.why: Section 2.5's errors in 0.1.0, where reads have no token (D15): /healthz and /v1/status answer; an unknown run or rank, a rank outside 0 to 99,999, a limit or page size out of range and an unknown column are refused as named.

cases.name: http_listen_flags
cases.why: Section 2.1: the listener is off unless asked for; --ui turns on 127.0.0.1:50052 when no address is given and serves the page; an address given wins; an address that is not loopback is refused in 0.1.0 whatever the token or --allow-unauthenticated.

cases.name: port_taken
cases.why: Section 2.1: when its port is in use the server stops, exit 1, with a line that names the address and --http-listen 127.0.0.1:0, for the default port and for one given.

cases.name: start_lines
cases.why: Section 2.1: on standard output after Flight's line, the bound address for scripts, the URL with its scheme, and under it the tunnel hint only when SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY is set and not empty.

cases.name: relative_urls
cases.why: Section 2.2: the page's relative paths stay under a proxy's prefix; a path from the root leaves it.

cases.name: series_keeps_spikes
cases.why: A spike of 50 at step 517 and a NaN at step 800 among 1,000 points of 1.0, cut to at most 100 points: both kept.

cases.name: series_short_is_whole
cases.why: A series no longer than the points asked for is returned whole, not downsampled.

cases.name: scan_pages_by_step_range
cases.why: Every row of [5, 20), the named column with the identity keys, six rows a page; no token after the last.

cases.name: scan_named_columns_only
cases.why: Only the columns named; a column some parts lack (an older part) is null in their rows.

cases.name: scan_resolved_attempts
cases.why: Attempt B resumed at step 6: the resolved scan leaves out A's steps 6 to 9; attempts=all keeps them, in the rank's attempt order.

cases.name: scan_view_changed
cases.why: A token after step 3: a new attempt that starts at or below it refuses the token; one that starts above it does not, and the next page reads the new resolved rows.

cases.name: read_stops_at_stored
cases.why: Parts through step 99, steps 100 to 120 held: a read returns through 99 and names both.

cases.name: scalar_series_merge
cases.why: WAVE_AL_CONTRACT.md section 4.6 in a read: at step 2 the scalar-only record of the highest seq wins; step 7 has no training record and is a point of its own; another name is not this series. On the base, today's evidence.scalar_series gives the resolved points (a pin); the read API must give the same.

cases.name: scalar_series_rolled_back
cases.why: B resumed at step 6: A's scalar-only point at step 8 is rolled back with A's training rows in the default read, and kept with attempts=all. On the base, today's evidence.scalar_series gives the resolved points (a pin); the read API must give the same.

cases.name: seq_watermark_after_compaction
cases.why: The seq watermark is the highest of the scalars-* names and the manifest's through_seq, so it survives an operator's delete of retired scalars-* objects.

cases.name: api_read_tokens
cases.why: 0.2.0, kept as written on Nov 24: with a token set, every path but /healthz is behind it, /metrics too; the errors behind a right token are 0.1.0's.

cases.name: host_allowlist
cases.why: Section 6.2.1: the loopback names with any port, without regard to case, and a name given with --allow-host; any other name is refused, and a missing Host or one that does not parse is a bad request (RFC 9112, section 3.2); an Origin must name an allowed host, Origin: null is refused, and a request with none passes; /healthz is not checked.

cases.name: framing_refused
cases.why: Section 6.2.1: until tensorquill.ui() exists every answer refuses to be framed, the refusals and errors included.

cases.name: snapshot_name
cases.why: A snapshot's key: the attempt, then the last step it read, at least eight digits.

cases.name: snapshot_usable
cases.why: Section 7.4, step 3: when the newest snapshot is used, with its tail, and why it is not.

cases.name: snapshot_restart_equals_replay
cases.why: The requirement of section 7.4: 300 steps stored with a snapshot after every part, a restart, 50 more; the report equals, byte for byte, the one a server with no snapshot gives on a copy of the same parts.

cases.name: compact_names
cases.why: Section 8.2's names, relative to the rank folder: never a part- name (D6).

cases.name: manifest_content
cases.why: 6,000 steps in 50-step parts: one compacted file of steps 0 to 4,999 from 100 inputs in manifest 1, the 20 parts above it the tail.

cases.name: compact_layout_change
cases.why: Protocol 4 parts then protocol 5 parts: the layout change closes the first group early, and the two are never one file.

cases.name: replay_manifest_first_order
cases.why: Manifest 2 cannot be read, so manifest 1 is the newest: A's compacted file, then A's parts above it, then B's parts; the compacted file no manifest lists, the scalar rows and the snapshot are not read.

cases.name: replay_compacted_file_missing
cases.why: A compacted file the manifest lists and the listing lacks is replaced by its inputs.

cases.name: manifest_race
cases.why: Two writers planned on manifest 1: the same group is written once and listed once; two groups end in manifests 2 and 3; a group manifest 1 already covers leaves its file unreferenced.

cases.name: orphan_after_crash
cases.why: A compacted file left by a crash before its manifest is never read; the next compaction reuses it when its inputs are the same, takes the next name when they are not, and writes its own when the groups differ.

cases.name: watermark_after_operator_delete
cases.why: The step watermark is the highest of the part- names and the manifest's through, so a store whose retired parts were deleted does not take steps 0 to 4,999 again; today's rule (`today_step`) would.

cases.name: load_records_reads_each_step_once
cases.why: A pin: every input kept, today's load_records reads part- objects only, so each of steps 0 to 249 once.

cases.name: load_records_after_operator_delete
cases.why: After an operator deletes the four retired inputs, load_records reads the manifest first and still gives each of steps 0 to 249 once; today it gives 200 to 249.

cases.name: outside_reader_glob
cases.why: An outside reader's glob: part-* reads each step once; *.parquet reads the compacted steps twice and takes the scalar rows in.

cases.name: retired_listing
cases.why: Grace 168 hours: the inputs of files listed 300 and 200 hours ago, manifest 1 (its successor is 200 hours old), the two older snapshots (the newest is 170 hours old) and the unreferenced compacted file; never the tail, the files listed, manifest 3 or the inputs of a file listed an hour ago.

cases.name: quota_scaled
cases.why: min(max(quota, streams x share), ceiling) at the proposed numbers.
